anf_compare.notes: No ANF or other public-domain English of this homily; translated from the Greek.

bible_refs.note: Exact quotation: Πᾶς ὅστις ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁμολογήσω κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.

choices.why: αἰσχύνομαι with the accusative means to feel shame before, to stand in awe of; Stephen honours his killers as the unwilling occasion of his crown.

choices.term: ὁμολογίας τῆς εἰς σὲ καὶ παρὰ σοῦ
choices.english: of confessing you and being confessed by you
choices.why: The phrase points ahead to Matthew 10:32: the martyr confesses Christ and Christ confesses the martyr.
rejected: of the confession made to you and given by you

choices.why: κρατήρ is a mixing bowl; 'bowl' keeps the image without adding a eucharistic 'chalice'.
κενόω is to empty; with blood into a bowl, 'poured out' is the natural English.

pass_a_gloss: [For even if] they sacrifice with evil reasoning, but nevertheless I feel shame before (respect) these, who [are] to me, even against intention, an occasion of the presence toward you, of the kingdom of the heavens, of the release from the clay, of the removal upward, of the victory of martyrdom, of the confession toward you and from you. For yours is the voice toward us, urged by which I readily gave myself over into sacrifice, and through the confession I emptied the blood into your hands as into a mixing bowl: 'Everyone who will confess in me before men, I too will confess in him before my Father who is in the heavens.' To him the glory unto the ages of the ages; amen.
pass_b_english: …they offer it with wicked intent, still I respect them, for even against their own purpose they are for me the occasion of coming into your presence, of the kingdom of heaven, of release from the clay, of being taken up on high, of a martyr’s victory, of confessing you and being confessed by you.

For yours is the voice that speaks to us; urged on by it, I readily gave myself up to sacrifice and, through my confession, poured out my blood into your hands as into a bowl: “Everyone who confesses me before men, I also will confess him before my Father who is in heaven” (Matthew 10:32). To him be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.
source_text:
πονηρῷ θύουσιν λογισμῷ, ἀλλ' ὅμως αἰσχύνομαι τούτους, οἵτινες ἀφορμὴ καὶ παρὰ
γνώμην ἐμοὶ τῆς πρὸς σὲ παρουσίας, τῆς τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείας, τῆς ἀπαλλαγῆς
τοῦ πηλοῦ, τῆς ἄνω μεταθέσεως, μαρτυρίου νίκης, ὁμολογίας τῆς εἰς σὲ καὶ παρὰ
σοῦ. Σὴ γάρ ἐστιν πρὸς ἡμᾶς φωνή, ᾗ προτραπεὶς ἐμαυτὸν ἑτοίμως εἰς θυσίαν
ἐπέδωκα, καὶ τὸ αἷμα καθάπερ εἰς κρατῆρα διὰ τῆς ὁμολογίας εἰς τὰς σὰς χεῖρας
ἐκένωσα· «Πᾶς ὅστις ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁμολογήσω
κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.» Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς
αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.

reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: The section opens mid-sentence: Εἰ γὰρ καί ('For even if…') ends the previous section. Stephen's first-person prayer, as Hesychius voices it, continues.
αἰσχύνομαι with the accusative means 'feel shame before, stand in awe of, respect' (LSJ); 'respect' chosen because Stephen honours his killers as the unwilling occasion of his crown.

ὁμολογίας τῆς εἰς σὲ καὶ παρὰ σοῦ: literally 'the confession toward you and from you'; it points ahead to Matthew 10:32 (the martyr confesses Christ, and Christ confesses the martyr), so rendered 'of confessing you and being confessed by you'.
κρατήρ is a mixing bowl; 'bowl' keeps the image without adding a eucharistic 'chalice'. Αὐτῷ in the doxology refers to Christ.
